name: EconLit
description: The American Economic Association's bibliography of economics journals, books, working papers and dissertations.
coverage: About 2 million records from 1886 onwards, with JEL codes and abstracts; available through EBSCOhost or ProQuest with a library subscription.
terms: Manual. EconLit is a subscription database reached through your library's EBSCOhost or ProQuest login; it has no API for individual users. Key writes the search in EBSCO syntax for you to paste.

steps: Open EconLit through your library (the library's database list, or EBSCOhost after signing in). Key opens EBSCOhost; you may need to sign in through your library first.
Choose Advanced Search, paste the search Key copied for you into the first box and leave the field menu on 'Select a field'.
Set the years and document types with the limiters on the page.
Select all results (add them to a folder), then Export, choose RIS, and save the file.
Write down the number of hits and the date for your search log.
manual.importHint: Save the export file, then drag it onto Key's library or choose File, Import. Key reads RIS, BibTeX and CSV files and merges duplicates with what you already have.

guide.summary: EconLit is the standard bibliography of economics, run by the American Economic Association. Most systematic reviews in economics search it. It needs a library subscription, so Key writes the search and you run it in EBSCOhost (or ProQuest).
guide.coverage: About 2 million records since 1886: journal articles, books, chapters, dissertations and working papers, all with JEL codes.
guide.fields: Key writes EBSCO field codes: TI title, AB abstract, KW author keywords, SU subject (JEL descriptors), AU author, SO journal, AF affiliation. Nn finds words within n words of each other.
limits: Needs your library's subscription and sign-in.
On ProQuest the field codes differ (ti(), ab()); adjust before you run the search.
tips: Export in batches of a few hundred records if EBSCOhost limits the export size.
